focus.label: Kaposi sarcoma
focus.why: The elderly patient's chronic violaceous atrophic calf plaque and biopsy showing band-like dermal vascular proliferation with CD34/CD31 positivity and D2-40 negativity are most consistent with Kaposi sarcoma; the pathologist identifies it as the most plausible vascular neoplasm. Confidence is 0.45 because HHV8 immunostaining is pending and bland endothelial cells without hemosiderin also allow a benign vascular proliferation.

payload.report: The elderly man's chronic enlarging violaceous atrophic calf plaque, unresponsive to topical steroids/antifungals, and biopsy showing band-like dermal vascular proliferation with CD34/CD31 positivity and D2-40 negativity most strongly support Kaposi sarcoma. The vascular immunophenotype and bland endothelial cells without hemosiderin or lymphoid atypia refute inflammatory dermatosis, chronic fungal infection, atrophic skin disease, and cutaneous lymphoma. Benign vascular proliferation remains less likely because of the progressive clinical course. Pending HHV8 immunostaining and T-cell clonality results prevent absolute certainty, but the current frontier is already a specific disease entity; no further refinement is needed.
